tasks.title: Fix G-3/G-4/G-5 in 03 (+05) acceptance-criteria consistency
tasks.description:
Targeted spec edits to reconcile EP-2 acceptance criteria with the contract and the actual architecture. Edit ONLY the US-2.1/US-2.2 region of idea-lab/final_requirements/03_acceptance_criteria.md and the EP-2 AC-themes line of idea-lab/final_requirements/05_prd_and_roadmap.md (~line 53). Do NOT rewrite whole documents; make surgical edits and preserve every header block, ID convention, and the [CONFIRMED]/[PROPOSED]/[ADJUDICATED] tags. If any fix would require changing a ratified DEC (DEC-4 status machine, DEC-11 par), STOP and report instead — you are aligning docs to ratified decisions, not changing them.

G-3 — ADD a missing US-2.1 acceptance scenario for the SETTLEMENT amount mismatch. Context: 03 US-2.1's 'Data validation & security' preamble already covers the REQUEST side (client-supplied amounts ignored/rejected; amount server-fixed at 10,000₮). What is missing is the SETTLEMENT side: the payment processor settles an amount != the 10,000₮ par (1,000,000 minor units). The OpenAPI contract declares 422 AMOUNT_MISMATCH for exactly this (paymentsWebhook / share-purchase settlement), and the money non-negotiable forbids posting a share for the wrong amount. Add a new numbered US-2.1 scenario (place it after the current Scenario 3 idempotency case, renumber the API-bypass scenario accordingly) along the lines of: Given a PENDING_PAYMENT application initiated a 10,000₮ purchase; When the processor's settlement webhook reports an amount != 10,000₮ (1,000,000 minor units); Then the settlement is rejected with 422 AMOUNT_MISMATCH, NO entry posts to the Membership Share Account, MembershipStatus remains PENDING_PAYMENT, and the mismatch is written to the audit log for reconciliation. Keep money as integer minor units, ₮ display, no float. Then update 05's EP-2 AC-themes line so its scenario COUNT matches 03's new total (it currently says '(03 EP-2, 16 scenarios)' — recount the EP-2 scenarios in 03 after your add and set the correct number) and so its '422 AMOUNT_MISMATCH' parenthetical now traces to a real 03 scenario.

G-4 — FIX 03 US-2.1's API-bypass scenario (currently 'Scenario 4 — Negative (security): API bypass attempt before KYC approval'). Its premise 'a client authenticated to an application with KycStatus = PENDING_REVIEW (so MembershipStatus = PENDING_KYC)' is architecturally unreachable: the share-purchase endpoint is MEMBER-authenticated (get_current_member, a verified member JWT), but a PENDING_KYC onboarding application is PRE-AUTH (it holds only a resume token, no Member row and no member JWT — a Member is only minted at KYC-approval -> PENDING_PAYMENT, DEC-4). So 'authenticated client at PENDING_KYC' cannot reach that endpoint. Preserve the SECURITY INTENT (the purchase endpoint must reject any caller not in PENDING_PAYMENT and must not initiate payment or post a ledger entry) but correct the premise to a REACHABLE one. Reframe to test the guard stated in 03 US-2.1's own preamble ('the purchase endpoint requires an application in MembershipStatus = PENDING_PAYMENT'): e.g. an authenticated MEMBER whose status is NOT PENDING_PAYMENT (already ACTIVE, or SUSPENDED) POSTs to the purchase endpoint -> 403, no payment initiated, no ledger entry, audit-logged; AND note that a pre-auth PENDING_KYC application cannot present member auth at all (so it is rejected at authentication, not at the status guard). Do not weaken the 403/no-payment/no-ledger/audit assertions.

G-5 — RECONCILE the illegal-transition error code. 03 US-2.2 Scenario 3 says the domain rejects an illegal transition with '409 Conflict'; the OpenAPI contract declares 422 ILLEGAL_TRANSITION for the analogous admin status-transition op. The contract is the single source of truth for HTTP status codes (clients build against it; changing the contract ripples across 192 ops). Therefore align 03 to the contract: change 03's illegal-transition code to 422 ILLEGAL_TRANSITION, keeping the rest of the scenario (naming from/to states, no partial state change) intact, and add a short parenthetical noting the code matches the contract's ILLEGAL_TRANSITION. Do NOT edit the OpenAPI contract. If you find a principled reason 409 is correct and 422 is the contract's error, do NOT silently pick one — leave 03 as-is and report the recommendation for a contract change instead.

ACCEPTANCE: run bash .softhouse/verify-docs.sh from repo root — HARD checks stay 0 and DRIFT must not increase vs baseline (your adds use ₮ / minor units, no $, no US rails/vendors, no first_name/last_name, no float). Handoff sections: ## Changes Made (quote each before/after) / ## Scenario recount (old vs new EP-2 count + how you counted) / ## Decisions / ## Sources / ## Unverified / ## Blockers / ## Follow-ups.

(G-4) the reframed API-bypass scenario has a REACHABLE premise and still asserts 403 + no payment + no ledger entry + audit; confirm the architectural claim (share-purchase endpoint is member-authed via get_current_member; a PENDING_KYC application is pre-auth with only a resume token) against backend/app/auth/deps.py and the onboarding/kyc services — a reframe that reintroduces an unreachable or a security-weakening premise is a REJECT. tasks.title: Fix G-6 — rename ShareStatus.MEMBER to match its wire value
tasks.description: CRITICAL CONTEXT — the backend application exists at backend/. Fix G-6: backend/app/models/membership.py defines ShareStatus with a Python-name/wire-value mismatch — the member MEMBER maps to wire value 'ISSUED' (ShareStatus.MEMBER = 'ISSUED'), while REDEEMED = 'REDEEMED' matches. This is a readability/footgun (a reader or a string comparison could assume name==value). GOAL: make the Python name match the wire value WITHOUT changing the stored/wire value and WITHOUT a migration. FIRST verify the canonical value: check how 04_technical_architecture.md defines E-5 MembershipShare.status (the enum's allowed values) and confirm the domain value is 'ISSUED' (a share that has been issued), not 'MEMBER'. If 04 says the value should be 'ISSUED' (expected), rename the Python member MEMBER -> ISSUED keeping the value string 'ISSUED' unchanged, and update EVERY reference to ShareStatus.MEMBER across backend/ (grep for 'ShareStatus.MEMBER' and for the bare string 'MEMBER' used as a share status). Because the stored value 'ISSUED' is unchanged, check_migration MUST still pass with NO new migration and NO schema drift — if it shows drift, you changed the value by mistake; revert to value-preserving. If instead 04 says the value should be 'MEMBER', STOP and report (that would be a value/migration change, out of this task's scope). Add/adjust a test only if an existing test pins the old name. ACCEPTANCE (run all, report each): cd backend && python3 -m pytest -q (full suite green); python3 -m app.db.check_models; python3 -m app.db.check_migration (MUST pass, no new migration); python3 openapi/validate.py. Scope: backend/app/models/membership.py + any files referencing ShareStatus.MEMBER (+ a test if needed). Handoff: ## Changes Made / ## Value-preservation proof (check_migration output) / ## References updated / ## Tests / ## Blockers / ## Follow-ups.
